correctness.rationale: Five distinct nodes give uniqueness: after multiplication by z^2, any trigonometric polynomial of degree two vanishing there becomes an ordinary polynomial of degree at most four with five distinct roots. The cardinal four-sine denominator is positive in the lifted cyclic order (four negative sine factors); integrating the constant moment gives the sum of three cosines divided by 8D. With half-gaps u,v,w the numerator is cos(u+2v+w)+2 cos(u)cos(w). For alpha<=alpha_*<1/4 the outside angle derivatives are strictly positive in a and negative in d, since u,w are in (0,pi/2) and u+2v+w in (0,pi). Thus the minimum uses a at its left endpoint and d at its right endpoint. Expanding the four inner corners gives the displayed three distinct expressions; the stated difference factors are positive for 0<pi*alpha/5<=pi/20 by the bounds on the sines. In either inner angle each term satisfies S''+S/4=0. On its interval the sine interpolation coefficients are nonnegative with sum at least one, and strictly positive in the interior. Consequently the nonnegative corner lower bound extends to the box, and at the threshold only the alternating corner gives zero; the target offset enters only D and can be arbitrary. The corner numerator strictly decreases on [0,1/2), is 1/2 at zero and 1-sqrt(5)/2<0 at 1/4, so the exact arccos root and the larger-radius negativity follow. Both the specified exactness and the comparison with conditioning are meant for the same dimensionless grid-spacing jitter. The exact formula is correct; the last printed decimal digit is a roundoff artifact: the value is 0.20145942246051052177..., not 0.2014594224605106.... The supplied verifier was inspected, not run. A separate 50-digit complex cardinal-polynomial coefficient calculation (python3 /workspace/review_checks.py 5) confirms the sign switch and unique alternating corner for the fixed unperturbed target; this finite check does not replace the interior proof.
